static_traits.name: Liu Tianyu
static_traits.family_status: Spouse (husband) has passed away; the husband was a salesman in his lifetime
static_traits.social_status: Having a few close friends to confide in, but not yet discussing cooking Fear with them; Social gatherings involving meals affected
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no previous history of psychological problem treatment or counseling experience
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression and coherent logic, able to concretely describe emotions and thoughts; high cooperation, but shows tension and worry when cooking is mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I lack confidence in cooking, leading to complete avoidance of cooking. After a failed dinner party, Persistent anxiety, fearing every cooking attempt will be terrible.
basic_info.core_demands: A persistent fear of failing at cooking has begun to affect my overall mood and daily life, so I hope to resolve this problem through counseling.
growth_experiences: A dinner party held at home carried high pressure from trying to please guests, and the meal failed badly. After the event, the client's cooking Self-efficacy dropped significantly, gradually forming the Anticipation that 'every cooking attempt will be terrible', with intense Anxiety and shame; subsequently started avoiding cooking as much as possible, relying more on pre-made food or takeout, and feeling affected in Social situations involving meals.

core_beliefs: If I cannot satisfy others, I am just a failure

special_situations.event: When Thinking about having to cook (whether for oneself or others)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try cooking again, I will definitely fail like last time and the result will be terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to avoid cooking, relying on prepared foods or takeout to reduce risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess up again; this time will be terrible too

special_situations.event: Attending Social gatherings involving meals (possibly needing to cook or bring a dish)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the dish is not good enough, others will judge me and think I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids joining parts that require cooking, reducing exposure in meal-related settings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone will look down on me because I do not cook well

special_situations.event: Recalling that failed dinner party and using it as a reference for the future
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure proves I will always fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses that failure as grounds to refuse further attempts in order to avoid being set back again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It was so bad last time; this proves I am not suited for cooking

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and appreciated through cooking
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged, humiliated, and negated by others after failing
defense_goal: Avoiding failure and judgment by Avoiding cooking, maintaining a fragile sense of self-worth

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough, failure-prone self (especially in the cooking domain)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about cooking again or facing social scenes involving meals
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting others' attention as potential criticism and negation, believing one will be humiliated if not perfect (transference: seeing others as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tending to respond with avoidance and alternatives, such as emphasizing continuing to use takeout or pre-made meals to 'stabilize one's mood first'. Cautious tone, few commitments to difficult tasks, using conservative wording (e.g. 'wait first' 'do not take risks').

manifestations: Reducing participation in meal-related Social gatherings out of fear of being judged for poor cooking
Avoiding cooking leading to fewer opportunities to share meals and interact with others
outcomes: Social withdrawal and Increased sense of alienation

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Presuming others will judge oneself for not cooking well
Attributing inner shame and Fear in meal-related scenarios to 'others will look down on me'

positive_force: Having the experience of 'anticipating failure but getting good results' at Work, showing the ability to complete tasks under pressure
Stable career performance, nursing Work not yet affected by this problem
Positive attitude, willing to seek help and try to change
Has a few friends to confide in (though not yet discussing cooking Fear)
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, fortune-telling, overgeneralization, and black-and-white thinking
Excessively concerned about others' evaluations, worrying about being judged and humiliated
Avoiding cooking and relying on pre-made meals/takeout, Reinforcing the Fear cycle
Low Self-efficacy in the cooking domain, negating one's own abilities

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Anxiety and avoidance toward cooking (almost never cooking, relying on takeout/pre-made meals instead)
antecedent: Thinking about having to cook (for oneself or for others)
Recalling that failed dinner party and inferring future outcomes from it
target_behavior.core_reason: Forming a catastrophizing and black-and-white cognitive framework after the failed dinner party, combined with high expectations of pleasing others and fear of judgment, leading to a significant drop in Self-efficacy
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible failure and judgment, reducing Anxiety and shame in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Eating habits affected, social participation declining, persistent Self-denial and worsening Anxiety, reduced quality of life
